statement_en: Let $X_n$ be independent random variables such that $$\mathbb{P}(X_n=1)=\frac{1}{n},\qquad \mathbb{P}(X_n=0)=1-\frac{1}{n}.$$ Then for every sufficiently small $\varepsilon>0$, $$\mathbb{P}(|X_n|\geq \varepsilon)=\frac{1}{n}\to 0,$$ so $$X_n\xrightarrow{\mathbb{P}}0.$$ However, since $$\sum_{n\ge 1}\mathbb{P}(X_n=1)=+\infty,$$ the second Borel-Cantelli lemma implies that $X_n=1$ infinitely often almost surely. Hence convergence in measure (or in probability) does not imply almost everywhere conv
